samples.summary: The `output` "regression guard for #660" cannot fail on the regression it claims to guard
samples.evidence: packages/cli/test/output.test.ts:157-164 comments itself as "Regression guard for #660" and asserts `output({a:1},'json')` prints the body. But the actual regression this PR fixes lives at the ~30 call sites that used to pass `opts.quiet` (e.g. packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:83, cells.ts:26). After the signature change, `output` unconditionally prints regardless of quiet, so the assertion holds trivially and would ALSO have held on the old code (which was called with quiet=false in this test's shape). If someone reintroduced suppression at a call site (`if (!opts.quiet) output(...)`) or re-added a defaulted `quiet` param, this test still passes. Nothing in packages/cli/test parses `--quiet` through a command action and asserts the body is still written to stdout — namespaces.test.ts:11 shows the createProgram()-based harness exists to do exactly that but only inspects option metadata. The comment's fallback claim ("a caller that tries to pass one fails to compile") is a type-level assertion never exercised by any test (no expectTypeError / ts-expect-error case).
searchedFor: glob packages/cli/test/** for a command/e2e-level suite

samples.summary: Deleted quiet test for `outputError` replaced by an unrelated case; the new "errors print even under quiet" contract is untested
samples.evidence: The diff removes `it('honors quiet by exiting 1 without emitting stderr')` and substitutes `it('stringifies non-Error throwables')` (packages/cli/test/output.test.ts:137-141), which exercises the pre-existing `String(error)` branch, not the changed behavior. The new documented contract in packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:44-51 — that the error envelope survives `--quiet` — has no test at any level: every remaining outputError test calls it directly with no quiet notion, and no command-level test runs a failing command with `--quiet` to assert stderr is non-empty and exitCode is 1. Net effect: a behavior change (quiet no longer silences errors) shipped with strictly less coverage of quiet than before.

samples.summary: The retained "progress notice" half of the new --quiet semantics is untested for the command-level notice sites
samples.evidence: root.ts now advertises `--quiet` as "Suppress progress notices (result body and errors still print)". The library-level notice gates are covered (docs-export.test.ts:279 for writeBinary, docs-content.test.ts:121, slides-content.test.ts:215), but the notices emitted directly from command actions — sheets-export.ts:52 `if (!opts.quiet) console.log('Exported to ...')` and docs.ts:291/306 — have no test file at all (no packages/cli/test/sheets-export.test.ts exists). Note also that sheets-export.ts:53 writes its notice to stdout via console.log, which the new doc comment says is reserved for the result body; nothing tests that stream choice either.

samples.summary: `output` format test duplicates an existing dispatcher assertion
samples.evidence: `it('honors the requested format')` asserts `output([{a:1}],'csv')` yields 'a\n1', which is the same assertion already made at packages/cli/test/output.test.ts:87 (`format(data,'csv')` contains 'a\n1'). It adds only the thin console.log wiring; harmless but not new coverage of the change under review.

verdict.reason: The "Regression guard for #660" at packages/cli/test/output.test.ts:157-164 calls output({a:1},'json') with two arguments and asserts the body is printed. Per docs/tasks/active/20260806-cli-quiet-preserves-body-todo.md:17-25, the pre-fix code was output(data, fmt, quiet) which early-returned only when quiet was truthy — so a two-argument call printed the body on the broken code as well. The assertion therefore holds regardless of whether the #660 bug is present, and formatter.ts:26-28 now has no quiet branch at all, making it unconditionally true going forward. Searching wide, no test anywhere exercises --quiet against the body path: the only quiet-bearing tests are slides-content.test.ts:215-220 and docs-content.test.ts:121-128 (both assert stderr notice suppression only) and docs-export.test.ts:273-306 (writeBinary's stderr notice, a different emitter). Repo-wide grep for "--quiet" outside node_modules finds no test file other than output.test.ts (the other test hits are `git --quiet` in scripts/agent). No backend e2e spec uses --quiet, no CLI test spawns the binary (no spawn/execFile/bin.js in packages/cli tests), and there is no ts-expect-error/expectTypeOf anywhere in packages/cli, so the comment's "fails to compile" fallback is never exercised. schema.ts:26/33 — the exact command in the issue's acceptance criteria — is covered only by a registry-level test (schema.test.ts), never through a command action. The changed behavior (quiet must not suppress the body/envelope) ships with a test that cannot fail on the regression it names.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: formatter.ts:44-58 documents that outputError is never gated by --quiet, but no test at any level exercises that. All four outputError cases (output.test.ts:115-141), including the new 'stringifies non-Error throwables' at 137-141, call outputError with a single argument and would pass equally under a quiet-gated implementation invoked without quiet — they cover the String(error)/errorCode branches, not the quiet contract. The only --quiet regression comment (output.test.ts:157-159) backs body-side tests only (160-169), and its 'fails to compile' claim has no backing assertion (no @ts-expect-error anywhere in packages/cli). Searched wide for a counterexample: repo-wide grep for quiet in test files yields only slides-content.test.ts:215-220, docs-content.test.ts:121-128/235-243, docs-export.test.ts:273-283, all of which assert quiet suppressing progress notices, never an error envelope; backend CLI e2e specs contain no quiet; the only createProgram consumers in tests (version.test.ts:10, namespaces.test.ts:11) assert structure/version and never parse a failing command; all CLI tests live under packages/cli/test. So a real behavior change (quiet no longer silences errors) ships with no meaningful test — major under the missing-tests rubric.
